notes: Tier 1 (direct curl + WebFetch) blocked by Cloudflare ('Attention Required! | Cloudflare' interstitial on robots.txt via curl, HTTP 403 on WebFetch for the maison/decor pages), so escalated to Tier 2: Playwright headless Chromium with a standard desktop UA, which rendered full SSR/DOM successfully for every URL fetched. robots.txt (fetched via Playwright, HTTP 200) is empty/has no Disallow rules, so no Claude-specific opt-out applies. Scoped to the Simons Maison (home decor) department, confirmed via breadcrumbs ('Home > ...') and the left-nav header 'Simons Maison' on every category page fetched, and via URL path /en/home-decor/... (not /women-clothing/ or /men-clothing/). Checked both English (/en/home-decor/...) and French-Canadian (/fr/maison/...) left-nav taxonomies on the Halloween and Christmas pages; the two mirror each other exactly. The site's left nav exposes one section titled 'Holidays & Celebrations' (FR: 'Fêtes et célébrations') containing exactly 7 children: Halloween Collection (c9537), Thanksgiving (c9539), Christmas Collection (c9582), Home Decor Gifts (c9550), Host & Hostess Gifts (c9551), Self-Care Gifts (c9552), Gift Ideas for Kids (c9553). The last 4 are generic gift-occasion categories with no holiday/seasonal association stated by the site (no Christmas/Halloween framing in title, breadcrumb, or copy) and were excluded per the 'seasonal products vs. seasonal category' boundary rule -- they are gift-shopping categories, not holiday categories. 'Holidays & Celebrations' itself is only a menu heading (its href aliases to the Halloween Collection URL, it has no distinct PLP/product count of its own), so it was not added as a grouping row. The 3 genuine holiday categories (Halloween, Thanksgiving, Christmas) are flat siblings in the nav with no further sub-category children listed anywhere (no level-3 nav, no distinct filter-facet sub-URLs), so each is recorded as a single leaf row, not a parent+children group. Quantities were read from the PLP's own 'categoryFilters-productCount' display and cross-verified against the categoryPager component's data-products attribute (which is computed from data-page-size x number of full pages + remainder, confirming it is a real total, not a display cap): Halloween data-products=198 (data-page-size=99, data-max=2 pages: 99+99=198); Thanksgiving data-products=198 (same page math: 99+99=198, independently confirmed as a distinct catId c9539/breadcrumb 'Thanksgiving', not a duplicate of the Halloween page); Christmas Collection data-products=300 (data-page-size=99, data-max=4 pages: 99+99+99+3=300 -- note the page also carries a 'max_per_page=300' URL-cap field that happens to equal 300, but the independently-computed pagination total of 300 rules out that being a coincidental truncation). Checked sitemap.xml -> sitemap index -> staticSitemap-en.xml, which only lists the homepage (not a usable enumeration source for this site). Attempted direct site-search URLs for 'valentine', 'easter', 'diwali', 'new-year' -- all redirected to the homepage (the site's search does not support a plain ?q= query param; a zero-result search is not treated as proof of absence per the task rules, so this was not relied on). Absence of Valentine's Day, Easter, Diwali, and New Year is instead established from the exhaustive, identical-in-both-languages left-nav category tree under Home Decor, which currently (early Sept 2026, in-season for fall/winter) presents only Halloween, Thanksgiving, and Christmas as holiday categories -- consistent with the site's seasonal rotation of this menu section.
